newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt trades in range, lacking new ideas.
newsitem.headline: German debt trades in range, lacking new ideas.

text.p: German debt traded largely in a range at the start of the week, lacking the necessary momentum to move either lower or higher after Friday's turbulent trading, dealers said.

"Today it was the same old story, pretty dull," explained one trader, saying Tuesday might be slightly more interesting as the market could react to more statements from a key U.S. central banker or upcoming economic data.
Today the market focused mostly on European central bankers seeking to brush off talk that Europe's planned monetary union might not begin on schedule, on January 1, 1999.
The March Bund futures contract closed Frankfurt trading up five basis points at 103.32 while the benchmark 10 year cash bond was at 103.31 after its previous close of 103.16.
On Friday the market tumbled amid rumours that European monetary union might be postponed by several years, giving more nations time to prepare for its start.
At a bankers' conference in Frankfurt, Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said he could not understand talk of a delay in monetary union and that such talk was nonsense.
Dutch central bank president Wim Duisenberg also said he was confident Germany would meet the entry criteria.

The Bund futures contract traded in a range between 103.45 and 103.19 today, and several dealers said a similar range could be seen on Tuesday morning, unless the market is busy reacting to U.S. Treasury market movements.

U.S. dealers were concerned that a strong U.S. purchasing managers report could prompt Fed chairman Alan Greenspan to deliver more hawkish comments at the second stage of his congressional testimony on Wednesday.
"We will just have to see how the U.S. reacts to Greenspan," added another dealer.
